pharm: Topically acting 5-aminosalicylic acid that reduces intestinal mucosal inflammation in inflammatory bowel disease.
quick: Follow product instructions; some taken with food, some without
Usually compatible; monitor infant for diarrhea
Caution; risk of renal impairment - monitor function
Renal function, CBC, signs of acute intolerance
summary: Mesalazine (5-aminosalicylic acid) is an aminosalicylate used to treat and maintain remission of mild-to-moderate ulcerative colitis and, in some forms, Crohn's disease. It acts locally on the intestinal mucosa to reduce inflammation. Different oral (delayed/extended release) and rectal (suppository, enema) formulations deliver drug to specific gut regions. It is generally well tolerated; the main concerns are renal impairment, a rare acute intolerance syndrome that mimics a colitis flare, and hypersensitivity.
indications: Induction of remission in mild-to-moderate active ulcerative colitis
Maintenance of remission of ulcerative colitis
Treatment of distal/left-sided ulcerative colitis and proctitis (rectal forms)
Maintenance therapy in selected Crohn's disease (formulation-dependent)

dosage.d: Delayed/extended-release products: 2.4-4.8 g/day in divided or once-daily dosing depending on brand
dosage.n: Dose and frequency are formulation-specific; do not crush/chew controlled-release units

dosage.d: 1 g (or per product) once daily at bedtime, retained overnight, for 3-6 weeks
dosage.n: Empty bowel before use; retain as long as possible

dosage.d: 1 g once daily at bedtime (or per product)
dosage.n: For disease limited to the rectum

admin: Swallow delayed- or extended-release tablets/granules whole; do not crush, break, or chew
Granule sachets are sprinkled onto soft food or taken as directed and swallowed without chewing
Take consistently with respect to food per the specific product instructions
For enemas, empty the bowel first, lie on the left side, and retain overnight
Maintain good hydration to reduce renal risk
moa: Mesalazine is the active 5-aminosalicylic acid moiety that acts locally on colonic and ileal mucosa rather than systemically. It is thought to modulate inflammatory mediators by inhibiting cyclo-oxygenase and lipoxygenase pathways (reducing prostaglandins and leukotrienes), scavenging reactive oxygen species, and dampening nuclear factor-kappa B signalling and inflammatory cell activity in the bowel wall.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to mesalazine, salicylates, or any formulation component
Severe renal impairment for some products (per labeling)
relative: History of mesalazine-induced acute intolerance syndrome
Pyloric stenosis (delayed release may be retained)
monitor: Renal function before and during therapy
Acute intolerance syndrome (cramping, bloody diarrhea mimicking flare)
Blood counts in patients with blood dyscrasia risk

preg: Generally considered acceptable for use in pregnancy when needed to control active inflammatory bowel disease, as uncontrolled disease itself poses fetal risk. Use the lowest effective dose; some products contain dibutyl phthalate-coated forms that are best avoided.
lact: Mesalazine and its metabolite pass into breast milk in small amounts; usually considered compatible with breastfeeding. Monitor the infant for diarrhea, which has rarely been reported.
renal: Renal impairment (including interstitial nephritis and rarely renal failure) can occur. Use with caution, assess renal function at baseline and periodically, and avoid in severe impairment unless benefit outweighs risk.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment; rare reports of hepatotoxicity exist. Monitor if clinical signs of liver injury develop.

major: Azathioprine / 6-mercaptopurine (increased myelosuppression risk - monitor blood counts)
moderate: Nephrotoxic drugs including NSAIDs (additive renal risk)
Warfarin (possible reduced anticoagulant effect - monitor INR)
minor: Antacids that raise gastric/intestinal pH may alter release of pH-dependent formulations
interactions.food: Take according to the specific product's food instructions; food can affect release of some formulations.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction; moderate alcohol use is acceptable.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause spuriously elevated urinary normetanephrine measured by certain liquid-chromatography assays.

monitoring: Renal function (creatinine/eGFR) at baseline and periodically
Symptom response and watch for acute intolerance syndrome
Complete blood count, especially with thiopurines
Liver function if hepatic symptoms occur
counsel: Swallow tablets/granules whole - do not crush or chew controlled-release forms
You may notice intact tablet shells in the stool with some brands; this is usually normal
Drink plenty of fluids and attend kidney-function blood tests
Report worsening cramps and bloody diarrhea soon after starting - this may be a reaction, not a flare
Do not stop maintenance therapy on your own even when you feel well
pk: Local effect builds over days to weeks
Mesalazine about 0.5-1.5 h; acetyl metabolite about 5-10 h
Supports once-daily to thrice-daily dosing by product
Store at room temperature; protect from moisture and excess heat
pearls: Acts topically on gut mucosa - matching the formulation to disease location is key
Acute intolerance syndrome can mimic a UC flare; stop the drug if suspected rather than escalating
Monitor renal function - interstitial nephritis is the most important systemic risk
Combine oral plus rectal therapy for left-sided/extensive disease to improve remission rates
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is nearly time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your usual schedule - do not double up.
overdose: Mesalazine has low systemic toxicity, but large overdoses can produce salicylate-like effects (acid-base disturbance, dehydration, electrolyte changes). There is no specific antidote; treatment is supportive with attention to fluid, electrolyte, and renal status.
